questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Rain water absorbs carbon(IV) oxide from the air and dissolves limestone. This process of chemical weathering is called
questions.explanation: It carves out the karst scenery of limestone regions.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: After a week of torrential rain, the whole hillside above a village gave way at once and buried the farms below. This rapid movement is a
questions.explanation: The hillside surrenders in a single moment.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The knife-edged ridge separating two adjacent glacial troughs is an
questions.explanation: The ice planed both valleys at once.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A tributary glacial valley whose floor stands high above the main trough after the ice melted is a
questions.explanation: Its stream now leaps as a waterfall.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The large boulder of rock carried far from its home by glacier ice and dumped on stranger ground is an
questions.explanation: Granite rests on sandstone far from any source.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The sharp, pointed mountain summit carved where several cirques cut back into one another is a
questions.explanation: Snowdon and the Matterhorn wear the shape.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A long, narrow lake occupying a glacial trough deepened below sea level after the ice retreated is a
questions.explanation: Windermere and Loch Ness lie in such troughs.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The almost level surface produced when a landmass is worn down by erosion over immense ages is a
questions.explanation: The land's old age, flat and low.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The lone resistant hill of rock left standing above a worn-down plain around it is a
questions.explanation: The hard core outlasts its softer surroundings.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The fine, yellowish, wind-deposited silt that mantles the plains of north-west China is
questions.explanation: Wind-blown dust settles into fertile soil.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The steep-sided desert valley that remains dry except immediately after rare storms is a
questions.explanation: The flash flood roars through and is gone.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The emigration of the best-trained doctors and engineers from a country in search of better pay abroad is called
questions.explanation: The nation's trained minds flow outward.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The small farm close to a city on which vegetables and flowers are grown for the daily urban market practises
questions.explanation: Its fresh produce races to the city each dawn.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: Farming in which a family grows food mainly to feed itself, with little or no surplus for sale, is
questions.explanation: The harvest feeds the household first.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A settlement deliberately sited on dry, raised ground above marshes and flood plains is a
questions.explanation: Its founders fled the wet ground below.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The position of a settlement in relation to other settlements, routes and surrounding regions is its
questions.explanation: It describes the settlement's address in the wider world.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A city that is far larger than any other city in its country and dominates its national life, as Lagos once dominated Nigeria, is a
questions.explanation: The head is far bigger than the body.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: A slope that faces the warm midday sun will enjoy warmer conditions than one in shadow. This influence of slope direction on climate is called
questions.explanation: Vineyards climb the sunny side of the valley.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: An area of low atmospheric pressure, with inward-spiralling winds and unsettled, showery weather, is a
questions.explanation: The weather map's trough of storms.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: When streams flow outward in all directions from the top of a dome-shaped highland, the drainage pattern formed is
questions.explanation: Like spokes from a hub the rivers run.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The daily mean temperature of a station is obtained by
questions.A: adding the maximum and minimum and dividing by two
questions.B: reading the thermometer at noon only
questions.C: averaging all hourly readings of sunshine
questions.D: subtracting the minimum from the maximum
questions.explanation: The day's heat and cold share one figure.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q: The wind-rose diagram of a weather station shows chiefly
questions.A: how often the wind blew from each direction
questions.B: the speed of the fastest gale
questions.explanation: Longer arms mark the steadier winds.
